clue.text: Descriptive of a wild cheetah?

parts.note: a cheetah is the quickest runner on land, and a wild one is angry, so the phrase for frantic, breakneck action describes it literally

explanation.surface: A naturalist hunts for the right words to describe an untamed big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hectic and energetic, here read literally as speedy plus enraged.

clue.text: Extra information provided from more remote army detachments

parts.note: more remote means further away
a detail is a small group of soldiers assigned to a particular duty

explanation.surface: A report passes on fresh intelligence gathered from outlying military units.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional particulars supplied later are what people call extra information.

clue.text: Making one's name as a writer

definitions.text: Making one's name as a writer

parts.words: Making one's name as a writer
parts.note: read literally, this is writing one's own name on a document, not becoming a famous author

explanation.surface: An author achieves fame through literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your autograph on a cheque or contract is literally writing your name.

clue.text: Little things to put in a manuscript

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor jots small details into a handwritten draft.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms are the tiniest particles of matter, so they are proverbially little things.

clue.text: Not a unique type of bridge

definitions.meaning: something not one of a kind has an identical copy
a form of the card game bridge in which the same hands are replayed by different players

explanation.surface: A card player observes that this kind of bridge is nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is not unique, and in the card game the same deals are replayed at several tables.

clue.text: See 1
Untrue statement about essential part of diet

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lie about what is vital in their meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is a necessary component of healthy eating.

clue.text: Increase support to control violence

parts.note: to rein is to restrain or control
force is physical violence

explanation.surface: Authorities send more backing to restrain a violent outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or bolster something is to add to its support.

clue.text: Poor cut of rock form

indicators.note: to form these words is to rearrange their letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: A geologist frowns at a badly shaped piece of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock form' looks like the definition together, but 'form' is the anagram signal working on POOR CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock exposed at the surface of the ground.

clue.text: Not a galley, but may be found in one

definitions.text: Not a galley, but may be found in one

parts.words: Not a galley, but may be found in one
parts.note: one kind of ship is powered by engines rather than oars, and a cooking pot of the same name sits in a ship's kitchen

explanation.surface: A vessel is contrasted with an oared ship yet turns up aboard one.
explanation.walkthrough: A galley is both an oared ship and a ship's kitchen: the answer is a powered boat and also a vegetable pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a powered boat and a pan for cooking vegetables in vapour.

clue.text: Give a party a new constitution, perhaps

definitions.text: Give a party a new constitution, perhaps

parts.words: Give a party a new constitution, perhaps
parts.note: a party here is a group, and giving it a new make-up is forming it again

explanation.surface: Political reformers rewrite their party's founding rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorganise or reassemble a body of people is to form the group again.

clue.text: Display anger when having a brush with someone

definitions.text: Display anger when having a brush with someone

parts.words: Display anger when having a brush with someone
parts.note: a brush with someone is a clash, and a brush also has stiff hairs, so the verb for bristling hair and taking offence fits both

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross during a minor confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the hackles in anger, like an animal's hairs standing up, matches the stiff fibres of a brush.

clue.text: Locks controller

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair, not canal locks or door locks, and a clip keeps them in place

explanation.surface: Someone operates the gates on a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip that holds tresses in place controls one's locks.

clue.text: It's socially acceptable in a class debate

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for a school class

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school
U stands for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: A pupil says something offensive during a classroom discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper-class, socially acceptable usage) goes inside FORM, a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or medium for public discussion.

clue.text: Just twice is correct

parts.note: two words that each mean just, joined by and, make a phrase meaning fitting and correct

explanation.surface: A grammarian insists that repeating a word is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means entirely fitting, built from two synonyms for fair or just.

clue.text: Pacific islander is a man with a can, perhaps

definitions.text: Pacific islander is a man with a can, perhaps

parts.words: Pacific islander is a man with a can, perhaps
parts.note: playfully read as a tin-carrying man, the clue describes someone from the large island south of Australia

explanation.surface: A South Sea native is pictured carrying a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Australian island state named after explorer Abel Tasman is from the South Pacific region.

clue.text: See 13
Prepares for a costume party?

parts.note: getting ready for a fancy-dress event means putting on an outfit

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready for a fancy-dress do.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on smart or fancy clothes is what one does before such an event.

clue.text: Elaborate metal work to stop a bit of play

parts.note: to dam is to stop a flow
taken as written
a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: Ornate metalwork is used to halt part of a theatre performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament steel with inlaid or etched patterns, a technique from Damascus, is to embellish metal.

clue.text: See 1
Cosmetic surgery's result hidden by mum

indicators.note: one piece is concealed inside the word for mother

parts.note: mama is an informal word for mother
an operation leaves a scar

explanation.surface: A mother covers up the evidence of an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark preparation applied to eyelashes is a kind of make-up.

clue.text: The Spanish weapon involved in the movement of arms

definitions.text: involved in the movement of arms

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
a bow is a weapon for firing arrows

explanation.surface: A Spanish weapon features in an arms deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement of arms' suggests weapons trading, but it is limbs bending.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint in the middle of each limb lets the forearm bend and move.

clue.text: Public vehicle licence

parts.note: not a permit to drive a bus but a ticket allowing one to ride on it

explanation.surface: A permit for operating a public transport vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel card lets the holder ride on buses, so it is a licence for public transport.

clue.text: The Navy get under way in short film

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'The Navy get under way in short film' (7) for WESTERN; no parse found (WRENS + ET anagram needs words the clue lacks) and a search of the exact text found nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: The Navy get under way in short film

clue.text: She's a vessel in the drink

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for the drink

parts.note: tea is a common drink
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A woman is described as a ship floating in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, but here it is tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a girl's given name, so a female, someone referred to by this pronoun.

clue.text: Trial trials

parts.note: trial cases that settle a legal principle, or test runs that are themselves trials

explanation.surface: A court hears a series of experimental proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal actions brought to set a precedent are cases used to try a point of law.

clue.text: Singer with half a score gets nothing right

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half is ten
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A vocalist with half the music sheet gets every note wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male vocalist with a high voice.

clue.text: Vessel is said to be en voyage

indicators.note: the clue tells us a spoken word gives the answer

parts.note: on a voyage means on a cruise

explanation.surface: A ship is reported to be travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruse is an old word for a small earthenware pot or jar.

clue.text: What it means to a barman

definitions.text: What it means to a barman

parts.words: What it means to a barman
parts.note: behind the bar, it in a gin and it is short for a sweet vermouth from Italy

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a word means to a bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub 'gin and it' is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar staff use it as shorthand for vermouth from Italy.

clue.text: Sort of roll made with herb and an American stuffing

indicators.note: one piece is packed inside another as filling would be

parts.note: sage is a herb
an gives A

explanation.surface: A bread roll is filled with herbs and a US-style stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: A SAUSAGE roll is a British snack of sausage meat baked in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry-wrapped snack of seasoned minced meat is one variety of roll.

clue.text: A help or hindrance in the works

definitions.text: A help or hindrance in the works

parts.words: A help or hindrance in the works
parts.note: a wrench helps in a workshop, while throwing one into the works wrecks the plan

explanation.surface: Something in a factory may assist or obstruct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A spanner in the works' is the British idiom for a disruption; Americans say a wrench.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a mechanic's tool, and the idiom makes it a disruption.

clue.text: Don't stop, although a person's upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keep going even if somebody is troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses every letter of PERSON'S, its S included.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue determinedly is to carry on without halting.
